    71	The architecture consists of the following components:
    72	
    73	#### Library
    74	Reflects the contents of a parsed bibtex files, including all comments, entries, strings, preamples and their metadata (e.g. order). 
    75	
    76	#### A Splitter
    77	Splits a bibtex string into basic blocks (Entry, String, Preamble, ...), with correspondingly split content (e.g. fields on Entry, key-value on String, ...).
    78	The splitter aims to be forgiving when facing invalid bibtex: A line starting with a block definition (`@....`) ends the previous block, even if not yet every bracket is closed, failing the parsing of the previous block. Correspondingly, one block type is "ParsingFailedBlock".
    79	
    80	#### Middleware
    81	Middleware layers transform a library and its blocks, for example by decoding latex special characters, interpolating string references, resoling crossreferences or re-ordering blocks. Thus, the choice of middleware allows to customize parsing and writing to ones specific usecase. Note: Middlewares, by default, no not mutate their input, but return a modified copy. 
    82	
    83	#### Writer
    84	Writes the content of a bibtex library to a `.bib` file. Optional formatting parameters can be passed using a corresponding dedicated data structure.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Comprehensive test to ensure the fix works and doesn't break existing functionality."""

from bibtexparser import parse_string

def test_original_issue():
    """Test the exact case from the issue description."""
    print("=== Testing Original Issue ===")
    bib_content = '''@CONTROL{REVTEX41Control}
@CONTROL{aip41Control,pages="1",title="0"}
'''
    
    library = parse_string(bib_content)
    entries = library.entries
    
    print(f"Found {len(entries)} entries")
    
    # Should have 2 entries
    assert len(entries) == 2, f"Expected 2 entries, got {len(entries)}"
    
    # First entry: REVTEX41Control with no fields
    entry1 = entries[0]
    assert entry1.entry_type == "control", f"Expected entry type 'control', got '{entry1.entry_type}'"
    assert entry1.key == "REVTEX41Control", f"Expected key 'REVTEX41Control', got '{entry1.key}'"
    assert len(entry1.fields) == 0, f"Expected 0 fields, got {len(entry1.fields)}"
    
    # Second entry: aip41Control with fields
    entry2 = entries[1]
    assert entry2.entry_type == "control", f"Expected entry type 'control', got '{entry2.entry_type}'"
    assert entry2.key == "aip41Control", f"Expected key 'aip41Control', got '{entry2.key}'"
    assert len(entry2.fields) == 2, f"Expected 2 fields, got {len(entry2.fields)}"
    
    field_dict = {f.key: f.value for f in entry2.fields}
    assert field_dict["pages"] == "1", f"Expected pages='1', got '{field_dict.get('pages')}'"
    assert field_dict["title"] == "0", f"Expected title='0', got '{field_dict.get('title')}'"
    
    print("✓ Original issue test passed")

def test_standard_entries_still_work():
    """Ensure standard entries still work correctly."""
    print("\n=== Testing Standard Entries Still Work ===")
    bib_content = '''@article{test2023,
  author = "John Doe",
  title = "Test Article",
  year = "2023"
}

@book{other2022,
  author = "Jane Smith",
  title = "Other Book"
}
'''
    
    library = parse_string(bib_content)
    entries = library.entries
    
    print(f"Found {len(entries)} entries")
    assert len(entries) == 2, f"Expected 2 entries, got {len(entries)}"
    
    # First entry
    entry1 = entries[0]
    assert entry1.entry_type == "article", f"Expected entry type 'article', got '{entry1.entry_type}'"
    assert entry1.key == "test2023", f"Expected key 'test2023', got '{entry1.key}'"
    assert len(entry1.fields) == 3, f"Expected 3 fields, got {len(entry1.fields)}"
    
    # Second entry
    entry2 = entries[1]
    assert entry2.entry_type == "book", f"Expected entry type 'book', got '{entry2.entry_type}'"
    assert entry2.key == "other2022", f"Expected key 'other2022', got '{entry2.key}'"
    assert len(entry2.fields) == 2, f"Expected 2 fields, got {len(entry2.fields)}"
    
    print("✓ Standard entries test passed")

def test_mixed_entries():
    """Test mixing CONTROL entries with standard entries."""
    print("\n=== Testing Mixed Entries ===")
    bib_content = '''@article{real2023,
  title = "Real Article"
}

@CONTROL{REVTEX41Control}

@book{another2022,
  title = "Another Book"
}

@CONTROL{controlWithFields,test="value"}
'''
    
    library = parse_string(bib_content)
    entries = library.entries
    
    print(f"Found {len(entries)} entries")

        assert entry.key == exp_key, f"Entry {i}: expected key '{exp_key}', got '{entry.key}'"
    
    print("✓ Mixed entries test passed")

def test_edge_cases():

"""Specific tests for CONTROL entry parsing fix."""

import pytest
from bibtexparser import parse_string
from bibtexparser.library import Library


def test_control_entry_without_fields():
    """Test that CONTROL entries without fields are parsed correctly."""
    bibtex_str = "@CONTROL{REVTEX41Control}"
    library: Library = parse_string(bibtex_str)
    
    assert len(library.failed_blocks) == 0
    assert len(library.entries) == 1
    
    entry = library.entries[0]
    assert entry.entry_type == "control"
    assert entry.key == "REVTEX41Control"
    assert len(entry.fields) == 0


def test_control_entry_with_fields():
    """Test that CONTROL entries with fields are still parsed correctly."""
    bibtex_str = '@CONTROL{aip41Control,pages="1",title="0"}'
    library: Library = parse_string(bibtex_str)
    
    assert len(library.failed_blocks) == 0
    assert len(library.entries) == 1
    
    entry = library.entries[0]
    assert entry.entry_type == "control"
    assert entry.key == "aip41Control"
    assert len(entry.fields) == 2
    
    field_dict = {f.key: f.value for f in entry.fields}
    assert field_dict["pages"] == "1"
    assert field_dict["title"] == "0"


def test_multiple_control_entries():
    """Test multiple CONTROL entries in one file."""
    bibtex_str = '''@CONTROL{REVTEX41Control}
@CONTROL{aip41Control,pages="1",title="0"}
@CONTROL{simpleControl}
@CONTROL{complexControl,field1="value1",field2="value2"}
'''
    library: Library = parse_string(bibtex_str)
    
    assert len(library.failed_blocks) == 0
    assert len(library.entries) == 4
    
    # First entry: no fields
    entry1 = library.entries[0]
    assert entry1.entry_type == "control"
    assert entry1.key == "REVTEX41Control"
    assert len(entry1.fields) == 0
    
    # Second entry: with fields
    entry2 = library.entries[1]
    assert entry2.entry_type == "control"
    assert entry2.key == "aip41Control"
    assert len(entry2.fields) == 2
    
    # Third entry: no fields
    entry3 = library.entries[2]
    assert entry3.entry_type == "control"
    assert entry3.key == "simpleControl"
    assert len(entry3.fields) == 0
    
    # Fourth entry: with fields
    entry4 = library.entries[3]
    assert entry4.entry_type == "control"
    assert entry4.key == "complexControl"
    assert len(entry4.fields) == 2


def test_mixed_entries():
    """Test CONTROL entries mixed with standard entries."""
    bibtex_str = '''@article{test2023,
  title = "Test Article"
}
@CONTROL{REVTEX41Control}
@book{manual2022,
  title = "User Manual"
}
@CONTROL{controlWithFields,param="value"}
'''
    library: Library = parse_string(bibtex_str)
    
    assert len(library.failed_blocks) == 0
    assert len(library.entries) == 4
    
    # Check entry types and keys
    expected_entries = [
        ("article", "test2023"),
        ("control", "REVTEX41Control"),
        ("book", "manual2022"),
        ("control", "controlWithFields")
    ]
    
    for i, (exp_type, exp_key) in enumerate(expected_entries):
        entry = library.entries[i]
        assert entry.entry_type == exp_type
        assert entry.key == exp_key


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_control_entry_without_fields()
    test_control_entry_with_fields()
    test_multiple_control_entries()
    test_mixed_entries()
    print("All CONTROL entry tests passed!")

    def _get_items(self) -> List[v.ListItem]:
        """
        Create the list of items inside the folder.

        Returns:
            list of items inside the selected folder
        """
        folder = self.folder

        list_dir = [el for el in folder.glob("*/") if not el.name.startswith(".")]

        if self.extentions:
            list_dir = [
                el for el in list_dir if el.is_dir() or el.suffix in self.extentions
            ]

        folder_list = []
        file_list = []

        for el in list_dir:

            if el.is_dir():
                icon = self.ICON_STYLE[""]["icon"]
                color = self.ICON_STYLE[""]["color"][v.theme.dark]
            elif el.suffix in self.ICON_STYLE.keys():
                icon = self.ICON_STYLE[el.suffix]["icon"]
                color = self.ICON_STYLE[el.suffix]["color"][v.theme.dark]
            else:
                icon = self.ICON_STYLE["DEFAULT"]["icon"]
                color = self.ICON_STYLE["DEFAULT"]["color"][v.theme.dark]

            children = [
                v.ListItemAction(children=[v.Icon(color=color, children=[icon])]),
                v.ListItemContent(
                    children=[v.ListItemTitle(children=[el.stem + el.suffix])]
                ),
            ]

            if el.is_dir():
                folder_list.append(v.ListItem(value=str(el), children=children))
            else:
                file_size = su.get_file_size(el)
                children.append(
                    v.ListItemActionText(class_="ml-1", children=[file_size])
                )
                file_list.append(v.ListItem(value=str(el), children=children))

        folder_list = humansorted(folder_list, key=lambda x: x.value)
        file_list = humansorted(file_list, key=lambda x: x.value)

        # Check if we should add parent navigation based on max_depth restriction
        add_parent_navigation = True
        if self.max_depth is not None and self.max_depth >= 0:
            try:
                # Calculate the relative depth from initial folder
                initial_parts = self._initial_folder.resolve().parts
                current_parts = folder.resolve().parts
                
                # Find common prefix
                common_length = 0
                for i, (init_part, curr_part) in enumerate(zip(initial_parts, current_parts)):
                    if init_part == curr_part:
                        common_length = i + 1
                    else:
                        break
                
                # Calculate depth: how many levels we are below the initial folder
                # If we're at or above the initial folder level, depth is 0 or negative
                initial_remaining = len(initial_parts) - common_length
                current_remaining = len(current_parts) - common_length
                relative_depth = current_remaining - initial_remaining
                
                # If relative depth >= max_depth, don't allow further upward navigation
                if relative_depth >= self.max_depth:
                    add_parent_navigation = False
            except Exception:
                # In case of any error in path resolution, allow parent navigation
                add_parent_navigation = True

        # Add parent navigation item if allowed
        if add_parent_navigation and folder != folder.parent:
            parent_item = v.ListItem(
                value=str(folder.parent),
                children=[
                    v.ListItemAction(
                        children=[
                            v.Icon(
                                color=self.ICON_STYLE["PARENT"]["color"][v.theme.dark],
                                children=[self.ICON_STYLE["PARENT"]["icon"]],
                            )
                        ]
                    ),
                    v.ListItemContent(
                        children=[v.ListItemTitle(children=[f".. /{folder.parent.stem}"])]
                    ),
                ],
            )
            folder_list.insert(0, parent_item)

        folder_list.extend(file_list)

        return folder_list

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Test for the new max_depth functionality in FileInput."""

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from sepal_ui import sepalwidgets as sw


def count_parent_navigation_items(items):
    """Count parent navigation items in a list of items."""
    count = 0
    for item in items:
        if hasattr(item.children[1].children[0], 'children') and \
           ".. /" in str(item.children[1].children[0].children[0]):
            count += 1
    return count


def test_max_depth_functionality():
    """Test the max_depth parameter functionality."""
    print("Testing max_depth functionality...")
    
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_root:
        tmp_path = Path(tmp_root)
        
        # Create test structure: root/a/b/c
        a_dir = tmp_path / "a"
        b_dir = a_dir / "b"
        c_dir = b_dir / "c"
        
        a_dir.mkdir()
        b_dir.mkdir()
        c_dir.mkdir()
        
        # Test 1: Default behavior (no max_depth)
        file_input_default = sw.FileInput(folder=b_dir)
        items = file_input_default._get_items()
        parent_count = count_parent_navigation_items(items)
        assert parent_count == 1, f"Default behavior should allow parent navigation, got {parent_count}"
        print("✓ Default behavior test passed")
        
        # Test 2: max_depth=0 (no upward navigation)
        file_input_0 = sw.FileInput(folder=b_dir, max_depth=0)
        items = file_input_0._get_items()
        parent_count = count_parent_navigation_items(items)
        assert parent_count == 0, f"max_depth=0 should restrict parent navigation, got {parent_count}"
        
        # Navigate to child - should still restrict
        file_input_0._on_file_select({"new": c_dir})
        items = file_input_0._get_items()
        parent_count = count_parent_navigation_items(items)
        assert parent_count == 0, f"max_depth=0 should restrict parent navigation everywhere, got {parent_count}"
        print("✓ max_depth=0 test passed")
        
        # Test 3: max_depth=1 (allow 1 level above initial)
        file_input_1 = sw.FileInput(folder=b_dir, max_depth=1)
        
        # At initial folder - should allow parent navigation

def update_complex_name(metadata, filename, suffix):
    """
    Insert `_rec-<magnitude|phase>` entity into filename if data are from a
    sequence with magnitude/phase part.

    Parameters
    ----------
    metadata : dict
        Scan metadata dictionary from BIDS sidecar file.
    filename : str
        Incoming filename
    suffix : str
        An index used for cases where a single scan produces multiple files,
        but the differences between those files are unknown.

    Returns
    -------
    filename : str
        Updated filename with rec entity added in appropriate position.
    """
    # Some scans separate magnitude/phase differently
    unsupported_types = ['_bold', '_phase',
                         '_magnitude', '_magnitude1', '_magnitude2',
                         '_phasediff', '_phase1', '_phase2']
    if any(ut in filename for ut in unsupported_types):
        return filename

    # Check to see if it is magnitude or phase part:
    if 'M' in metadata.get('ImageType'):
        mag_or_phase = 'magnitude'
    elif 'P' in metadata.get('ImageType'):
        mag_or_phase = 'phase'
    else:
        mag_or_phase = suffix

    # Determine scan suffix
    filetype = '_' + filename.split('_')[-1]

    # Insert rec label
    if not ('_rec-%s' % mag_or_phase) in filename:
        # If "_rec-" is specified, prepend the 'mag_or_phase' value.
        if '_rec-' in filename:
            raise BIDSError(
                "Reconstruction label for images will be automatically set, "
                "remove from heuristic"
            )

        # Insert it **before** the following string(s), whichever appears first.
        for label in ['_dir', '_run', '_mod', '_echo', '_recording', '_proc', '_space', filetype]:
            if (label == filetype) or (label in filename):
                filename = filename.replace(
                    label, "_rec-%s%s" % (mag_or_phase, label)
                )
                break
